analyst.summary: Asian Paints' Q4FY26 recovery (PAT +69% YoY, double-digit decorative volume growth, margin expansion to 19.4% consolidated PBDIT) is real in magnitude but substantially explained by an easy year-ago comp (Q4FY25 had a Rs 183cr exceptional impairment and a genuine demand trough) and raw-material cost deflation that management says has more room to run into H2FY27 - not clear proof the two-year Birla Opus share war has been won back. Decorative volume still grew faster than value in the same 'recovery' quarter, tier-2/3 share loss to Birla Opus continued (Opus +7pp, AP -5pp), a newly Akzo-acquired JSW Dulux adds a fourth well-funded competitor from December 2025, and the CCI's abuse-of-dominance investigation (opened July 2025, Supreme Court declined to stay it in October 2025) remains unresolved. At ~59x trailing earnings - essentially unchanged from AP's pre-disruption historical premium of 55-75x - a reverse-DCF implies the market is pricing ~9-10% perpetual growth against 5.1% delivered in FY26 and a 1.0% trailing 3-year CAGR. That gap, layered on a structurally tougher four-player market and an open regulatory overhang, is not adequately priced in. Sell, with the honest caveat that this is a real judgment call: Q4 was a genuine beat and sell-side targets are split, not uniformly bearish.
